chunks: 919 - Al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān mentioned from al-Riḍā عليه السلام:

"Another reason is that the takbirs at the beginning of the salat (prayer) became seven because the original basis of the salat is two rak'ahs, and their opening is with seven takbirs: the takbir of the opening, the takbir of ruku', the two takbirs of the two sajdahs in the first rak'ah, then the takbir of ruku' in the second, and the two takbirs of the two sajdahs. So if a person says seven takbirs at the beginning of a salat, then afterward forgets something from the takbirs of the opening or is heedless regarding them, no deficiency enters upon his salat."

key_terms.أَوَّلِ الصَّلَاةِ: the beginning portion of the salat (prayer)
key_terms.التَّكْبِيرَاتُ: the declarations of 'Allāhu akbar' recited in the prayer opening
key_terms.السَّجْدَتَيْنِ: the two prostrations within a rak'ah
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَةِ الِافْتِتَاحِ: the opening takbir by which entry into the prayer begins
key_terms.رَكْعَتَانِ: the two units that form the original basis of the prayer
key_terms.نَقْصٌ: deficiency or shortcoming affecting the prayer

ai.seo_question: Why are there seven takbirs at the beginning of the prayer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام explains the rationale for seven opening takbirs in salat (prayer) by relating them to the foundational structure of the two-rak'ah prayer. The report shows that these takbirs serve as a complete opening framework, such that forgetting one later does not render the prayer deficient.
